studies.title: Engineered Probiotic Saccharomyces boulardii Reduces Colitis-Associated Colorectal Cancer Burden in Mice.
studies.abstract: Individuals with inflammatory bowel diseases experience an elevated risk of colorectal cancer driven by chronic inflammation. Current systemic immunosuppressive therapies often cause severe side effects. Live oral biotherapeutics are an emerging treatment modality that directly target the intestines. We have engineered a probiotic Saccharomyces boulardii strain that expresses targeting ligands to bind fibronectin on inflamed mucosa and secretes anti-tumor necrosis factor nanobodies locally to reduce inflammation. We previously demonstrated that engineering S. boulardii to bind fibronectin enhanced colonization and reduced inflammation in a DSS colitis model. Here, we tested the anti-cancer potential of engineered S. boulardii using a well-established model of IBD-associated CRC, azoxymethane-treated interleukin 10-deficient (AOM/Il10 Mice were orally administered engineered S. boulardii at two dosing frequencies, unmodified S. boulardii, or placebo throughout the 18-week model. Colons were harvested for gross, histological, and molecular evaluation for inflammation and tumorigenesis. Histological colon inflammation was reduced by twice weekly dosing of engineered and unmodified S. boulardii. Engineered S. boulardii reduced gross tumor number in a dose-dependent manner, with median tumor counts reduced from 7.5 to 2 per mouse (p < 0.0002 vs. placebo). Unmodified S. boulardii similarly reduced gross tumor number. Colonization studies revealed that engineered S. boulardii failed to colonize for greater time or density vs. unmodified S. boulardii. Together our data indicate that engineering S. boulardii does not reduce its ability to decrease inflammation-associated tumorigenesis, and that further host-binding target optimization is required to enhance colonization and anti-cancer effects.

studies.title: Saccharomyces Boulardii alleviates neuroinflammation and oxidative stress in PTZ-kindled seizure rat model.
studies.abstract: Previous research have reported that modulating the gut microbiome composition by fecal microbiota transplantation and probiotic administration can alleviate seizure occurrence and severity. Saccharomyces boulardii (SB) is a yeast probiotic that has demonstrated ameliorating effects on anxiety, memory and cognitive deficit, and brain amyloidogenesis. Experimental validation of 28 communities highlighted the role of S. boulardii as a key player in microbial communities, significantly boosting the community's cell number and production of anti-inflammatory effectors, thereby affirming its essential role in improving symbiotic dynamics. Based on our observation, one defined community significantly activated the aryl hydrocarbon receptor-a key regulator of immune response-280-fold more effectively than the community without S. boulardii. This study underscores the potential of microbial communities for the design of more effective probiotic formulations.

studies.title: Effects of Saccharomyces boulardii on microbiota composition and metabolite levels in the small intestine of constipated mice.
studies.abstract: Saccharomyces boulardii (S. boulardii) is a fungal probiotic used to treat digestive disorders. However, the mechanism(s) by which S. boulardii affects the small intestine remains unclear. Here, we aimed to explore the effects of S. boulardii on the small intestine and the underlying mechanisms in mice with loperamide-induced constipation. While S. boulardii administration did not fully reverse the alterations in loperamide-induced defecation parameters, it altered the small intestinal floral composition toward a community conducive to alleviate constipation. Moreover, S. boulardii up-regulated the expression of tyrosine-protein kinase Kit (c-Kit), aquaporin 3 (AQP3), interleukin (IL)-10, myosin light chain kinase (MLCK), and phosphorylated myosin light chain 20 (P-MLC20), while concurrently down-regulating the expression levels of inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS), p65, and IL-17 A. These alterations indicate a discernible effect of small intestinal water reabsorption, inflammatory factor levels, and smooth muscle contraction. Saccharomyces boulardii also positively regulated small intestinal metabolite levels, such as fructose 6-phosphate, dihomo-alpha-linolenic acid, and 3-(4-hydroxyphenyl) lactate, and participated in metabolic pathways such as arginine biosynthesis, linoleic acid metabolism, and protein digestion and absorption. While not fully reversing defecation changes, Saccharomyces boulardii alters intestinal flora, up-regulates key proteins affecting water reabsorption and inflammation, and positively influences metabolic pathways. Our study provides serves as a basis for further studies on the application of S. boulardii in the treatment of intestinal disorders.

studies.title: Protective effects of Saccharomyces boulardii CNCM I-745 in an experimental model of NSAID-induced enteropathy.
studies.abstract: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) induce a broad spectrum of gastro-intestinal adverse effects, including ulceration and bleeding. The pathophysiology of NSAID enteropathy is complex and incompletely understood, but some evidence showed that NSAIDs impair the intestinal barrier and cause a gut dysbiosis. Identifying new treatments aiming to reverse or attenuate NSAID-induced adverse effects would have a significant impact on a high number of patients. The aim of this work is to assess the effects of the probiotic yeast Saccharomyces boulardii CNCM I-745 (Sb) on a model of NSAID-induced enteropathy. Four groups of mice were tested: Control, Indomethacin, Sb, and Sb + Indomethacin. A clinical score was evaluated throughout the experiment. Faecal calprotectin, microbiota and haemoglobin analyses were performed. At the end of the treatments, the small intestine, colon, and caecum lengths, and intestinal permeability were measured. Sections of ileum and jejunum were observed to assess a histological score and ileal cytokines were measured by immunoassay. Indomethacin-treated animals showed an increase in their clinical scores, reflecting a worsening of their general state. Mice co-treated with Sb and indomethacin displayed an improvement of their clinical score in comparison with mice treated with indomethacin alone. Sb prevented the indomethacin-induced shortening of the small intestine and caecum, and significantly attenuated the severity of intestinal lesions. Sb also prevented the increase in faecal calprotectin, reduced faecal haemoglobin, and prevented the increase of intestinal permeability in mice treated with indomethacin. Sb also counteracted the increase of faecal bacteria associated with the pathogenesis of NSAID-enteropathy. In conclusion, our results show a protective effect of Sb in a model of indomethacin-induced enteropathy. Sb improved the intestinal barrier function and exerted a positive action on gut microbiota composition.

studies.title: Saccharomyces boulardii improves the behaviour and emotions of spastic cerebral palsy rats through the gut-brain axis pathway.
studies.abstract: Cerebral palsy (CP) is a kind of disability that influences motion, and children with CP also exhibit depression-like behaviour. Inflammation has been recognized as a contributor to CP and depression, and some studies suggest that the gut-brain axis may be a contributing factor. Our team observed that Saccharomyces boulardii (S. boulardii) could reduce the inflammatory level of rats with hyperbilirubinemia and improve abnormal behaviour. Both CP and depression are related to inflammation, and probiotics can improve depression by reducing inflammation. Therefore, we hypothesize that S. boulardii may improve the behaviour and emotions of spastic CP rats through the gut-brain axis pathway. Our new rat model was produced by resecting the cortex and subcortical white matter. Seventeen-day-old CP rats were exposed to S. boulardii or vehicle control by gastric gavage for 9 days, and different behavioural domains and general conditions were tested. Inflammation was assessed by measuring the inflammatory markers IL-6 and TNF-α. Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activity was assessed by measuring adrenocorticotropic hormone and corticosterone in the serum. Changes in the gut microbiome were detected by 16S rRNA. The hemiplegic spastic CP rats we made with typical spastic paralysis exhibited depression-like behaviour. S. boulardii treatment of hemiplegic spastic CP rats improves behaviour and general conditions and significantly reduces the level of inflammation, decreases HPA axis activity, and increases gut microbiota diversity. The model developed in this study mimics a hemiplegic spastic cerebral palsy. Damage to the cortex and subcortical white matter of 17-day-old Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats led to spastic CP-like behaviour, and the rats exhibited symptoms of depression-like behaviour. Our results indicate that S. boulardii might have potential in treating hemiplegic spastic CP rat models or as an add-on therapy via the gut-brain axis pathway.

studies.title: Probiotic Saccharomyces boulardii Alleviates Lung Injury by Reduction of Oxidative Stress and Cytokine Response Induced by Supraceliac Aortic Ischemia-Reperfusi
studies.abstract: Ischemia-reperfusion injury is an important cause of multiple organ failure in cardiovascular surgery. Our aim is to investigate the effect of the probiotic Saccharomyces boulardii on oxidative stress, inflammatory response, and lung injury in an experimental model of aortic clamping. Twenty-one Wistar rats were randomized into three groups (n=7). Control group animals received saline gavage for a week before undergoing median laparotomy. In other groups, supraceliac aorta was clamped for 45 minutes to induce ischemia followed by reperfusion for 60 minutes. In the ischemiareperfusion group, saline gavage was given preoperatively for one week. Ischemia-reperfusion+probiotic group rats received probiotic gavage for seven days before aortic clamping. The levels of oxidative stress markers and pro-inflammatory cytokines were determined in both serum and lung tissue samples. Ileum and lung tissues were harvested for histological examination. Ischemia-reperfusion caused severe oxidative damage and inflammation evident by significant increases in malondialdehyde and cytokine levels (tumor necrosis factor alpha and interleukin-1 beta) and decreased glutathione levels in both serum and lung tissues. There was severe histological tissue damage to the lung and ileum in the ischemia-reperfusion group. Probiotic pretreatment before aortic clamping caused significant suppression of increases in serum and lung tissue malondialdehyde and tumor necrosis factor alpha levels. Histological damage scores in tissue samples decreased in the ischemia-reperfusion+probiotic group (P<0,005). Oral supplementation of probiotic S. boulardii before supraceliac aortic ischemia-reperfusion in rats alleviates lung injury by reducing oxidative stress, intestinal cellular damage, and modulation of inflammatory processes.

studies.title: Mechanism and therapeutic effects of Saccharomyces boulardii on experimental colitis in mice.
studies.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a type of chronic inflammatory disturbance that affects a number of individuals worldwide; the precise mechanism is unclear and treatment is frequently insufficient to maintain patients in remission. Saccharomyces boulardii is a thermophilic, non‑pathogenic yeast that may be administered for prophylaxis and treatment of a variety of diarrheal diseases. Recent clinical studies have demonstrated that it may have a role in IBD; however, the mechanism of action is unclear. The hypoxia‑inducible factors (HIFs) are ubiquitously expressed regulators of cellular adaptation to hypoxia and are central to the adaptive and inflammatory responses of cells of the intestinal mucosa in patients with IBD. The present study aimed to investigate the effects of S. boulardii on dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)‑induced colitis in mice and the effects of S. boulardii on HIFs. Mice were divided into five groups (n=10 mice/group): i) Control; ii) DSS; iii) S. boulardii (Sb) + DSS; iv) normal saline (NS) + DSS; and v) Sb. For 14 consecutive days, mice from the Sb+DSS and Sb groups were given S. boulardii suspension in saline (150 mg/kg/day; final volume 0.2 ml) by oral gavage. The NS+DSS group received the same volume of NS by gavage. The Control mice received water only. From day 8 to day 14, 3.5% DSS was added to the drinking water of the DSS, Sb+DSS and NS+DSS groups to induce acute colitis. Body weight decreased and disease activity index and histological score increased in mice with DSS‑induced colitis. Oral administration of S. boulardii reduced DSS‑induced weight loss, ameliorated the histological damage and protected the colon barrier in mice with DSS‑induced colitis. The expression of HIF‑1α and HIF‑2α in colon tissues was measured by reverse transcription‑quantitative polymerase chain reaction, immunoblotting and immunohistochemistry. The increase in HIFs in the colon induced by DSS was significantly inhibited by S. boulardii treatment. The expression levels of several epithelial‑mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers and of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) that are regulated by HIFs were measured. S. boulardii reduced EMT and decreased expression of VEGF that was induced by DSS treatment. These results indicated that treatment with S. boulardii ameliorated DSS‑induced colitis, partly through downregulation of HIF‑1α and HIF‑2α.

studies.title: Saccharomyces boulardii improves humoral immune response to DNA vaccines against leptospirosis.
studies.abstract: Saccharomyces boulardii may improve the immune response by enhancing the production of anti-inflammatory cytokines, T-cell proliferation and dendritic cell activation. The immunomodulator effect of this probiotic has never been tested with DNA vaccines, which frequently induce low antibody titers. This study evaluated the capacity of Saccharomyces boulardii to improve the humoral and cellular immune responses using DNA vaccines coding for the leptospiral protein fragments LigAni and LigBrep. BALB/c mice were fed with rodent-specific feed containing 108 c.f.u. of Saccharomycesboulardii per gram. Animals were immunized three times intramuscularly with 100 µg of pTARGET plasmids containing the coding sequences for the above mentioned proteins. Antibody titers were measured by indirect ELISA. Expression levels of IL-4, IL-10, IL-12, IL-17, IFN-γ and TGF-β were determined by quantitative real-time PCR from RNA extracted from whole blood, after an intraperitoneal boost with 50 µg of the recombinant proteins.Results/Key findings. Antibody titers increased significantly after the second and third application when pTARGET/ligAni and pTARGET/ligBrep were used to vaccinate the animals in comparison with the control group (P<0.05). In addition, there was a significant increase in the expression of the IL-10 in mice immunized with pTARGET/ligBrep and fed with Saccharomyces boulardii. The results suggested that Saccharomyces boulardii has an immunomodulator effect in DNA vaccines, mainly by stimulating the humoral response, which is often limited in this kind of vaccine. Therefore, the use of Saccharomyces boulardii as immunomodulator represents a new alternative strategy for more efficient DNA vaccination.

studies.title: Saccharomyces boulardii CNCM I-745 supplementation reduces gastrointestinal dysfunction in an animal model of IBS.
studies.abstract: We evaluated the effect of Saccharomyces boulardii CNCM I-745 on intestinal neuromuscular anomalies in an IBS-type mouse model of gastrointestinal motor dysfunctions elicited by Herpes Simplex Virus type 1 (HSV-1) exposure. Mice were inoculated intranasally with HSV-1 (102 PFU) or vehicle at time 0 and 4 weeks later by the intragastric (IG) route (108 PFU). Six weeks after IG inoculum, mice were randomly allocated to receive oral gavage with either S. boulardii (107 CFU/day) or vehicle. After 4 weeks the following were determined: a) intestinal motility using fluorescein-isothiocyanate dextran distribution in the gut, fecal pellet expulsion, stool water content, and distal colonic transit of glass beads; b) integrity of the enteric nervous system (ENS) by immunohistochemistry on ileal whole-mount preparations and western blot of protein lysates from ileal longitudinal muscle and myenteric plexus; c) isometric muscle tension with electric field and pharmacological (carbachol) stimulation of ileal segments; and d) intestinal inflammation by levels of tumor necrosis factor α, interleukin(IL)-1β, IL-10 and IL-4. S. boulardii CNCM I-745 improved HSV-1 induced intestinal dysmotility and alteration of intestinal transit observed ten weeks after IG inoculum of the virus. Also, the probiotic yeast ameliorated the structural alterations of the ENS induced by HSV-1 (i.e., reduced peripherin immunoreactivity and expression, increased glial S100β protein immunoreactivity and neuronal nitric oxide synthase level, reduced substance P-positive fibers). Moreover, S. boulardii CNCM I-745 diminished the production of HSV-1 associated pro-inflammatory cytokines in the myenteric plexus and increased levels of anti-inflammatory interleukins. S. boulardii CNCM I-745 ameliorated gastrointestinal neuromuscular anomalies in a mouse model of gut dysfunctions typically observed with irritable bowel syndrome.

studies.title: Saccharomyces boulardii and Bacillus subtilis B10 modulate TLRs and cytokines expression patterns in jejunum and ileum of broilers.
studies.abstract: The present study was designed to evaluate the effects of Saccharomyces boulardii (Sb) and Bacillus subtilis B10 (Bs) on intestinal epithelial Toll like receptors (TLR), and Cytokine expression response to understand the intestinal epithelial innate immune mechanism in broilers. A total of 300 birds (Sanhuang broilers) were allotted into three groups (n = 100) and each divided into five replications (n = 20). Control group (Ctr) birds were fed basal diet, broilers in experimental groups received (1×108cfu/kg feed) Sb and Bs respectively in addition to basal diet for 72 days. The result showed significant increase in mRNA expression level of TLR2, TLR4 and TLR15. Down streaming MyD88, TRAF6, TAB2 and NF-κB mRNA level noted higher, in the jejunum and ileum as compared to control group. Meanwhile, IL-6, TNFα, IL-10, TGF-β expression levels showed high expression in the jejunum of Sb and Bs groups. IL-10 expression level increased in the ileum and IL-6, TNFα, IL-10 and TGF-β expression levels increased in the jejunum of Sb group. Levels of IL-1 β, IL-17, and IL-4, increased merely in Sb group. Ileal cytokines IL-1β, IL-17 and IL-4concentration were noted higher in Sb group, and IL-1β, and IL-4 levels were up-regulated in Bs group. The results indicated that the INF-γ and IL-8 level decreased in Sb and BS groups. Serum IgA and sIgA level increased in both treatment groups. Our findings illustrated that S. boulardii and B. subtilis B10 may have a role to induce mucosal immunity by activating the TLRs and cytokines expressions in broilers.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A beneficial yeast strain used as a live probiotic supplement for gut health.
explanation.what_it_is: Saccharomyces boulardii is a strain of baker's yeast—a single-celled fungus—that survives passage through your stomach and settles in the small intestine. Unlike most probiotics, which are bacteria, this is a yeast. It's taken as a live supplement in capsule or powder form, often freeze-dried so the cells remain viable until they reach your gut.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Secretes compounds that reduce harmful bacteria and calm intestinal inflammation.
explanation.how_it_works: The yeast produces substances that inhibit or kill pathogenic (disease-causing) bacteria—notably Helicobacter pylori, which causes stomach ulcers—and releases molecules that quiet the inflammatory response in your gut lining. It also appears to strengthen the barrier between your intestinal cells, reducing 'leaky gut' where unwanted particles cross into the bloodstream. Additionally, it may shift the composition of your microbiota (the trillions of microbes in your gut) toward a healthier balance, and some evidence suggests it boosts the activity of immune cells that live in the gut wall. The exact mechanisms are not fully mapped, but the pattern across studies points to both direct antimicrobial action and immune-dampening effects.
explanation.safety_line: Well-tolerated in short-term trials; long-term safety and risks in specific populations remain untested.
explanation.safety_detail: The human trials retrieved reported mild or no adverse events; most studies lasted weeks to a few months. However, trials enrolled only healthy adults and some specific patient groups (e.g., H. pylori-infected patients, heart failure patients), and none adequately addressed long-term use beyond a few weeks. Saccharomyces boulardii is a live organism, and the safety profile in immunocompromised individuals, pregnancy, and breastfeeding remains unknown.
safety_bullets: Immunocompromised patients (advanced HIV, on immunosuppressants for organ transplant): untested; theoretical risk of yeast infection is not established in trials.
Pregnancy and breastfeeding: no human trials retrieved; safety unknown.
Drug interactions with azole antifungals (e.g., fluconazole): not reported in retrieved trials; potential for direct antagonism is unexamined.
Pediatric safety: one trial in neonates (newborns) found benefit for jaundice, but broader use in children and adolescents is poorly studied.
explanation.chem_meaning: Saccharomyces boulardii is a large, complex organism (a eukaryotic cell, meaning it has a nucleus and organelles like your own cells do), so it does not behave like a small drug molecule. It is not absorbed; it lives in your gut lumen and is eventually shed. The bioactive compounds it produces—short-chain fatty acids, antimicrobial peptides, and immune-signaling molecules—are what actually enter your bloodstream, while the yeast itself remains local to the intestine.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Six human trials and a 2025 meta-analysis examined the yeast's effect on digestion, H. pylori eradication, neonatal jaundice, irritable bowel syndrome, and heart failure. Studies ranged from small open-label trials (n=21) to a large RCT (n=151). When added to antibiotic therapy for H. pylori, the yeast improved eradication rates and microbiota recovery. One RCT (n=119) in newborns found it reduced jaundice severity. A trial in diarrhea-predominant IBS (n=21) reported clinical improvement. The 2021 heart failure trial (n=151) found benefit, though heart failure is not classically a 'digestion' outcome. Results are consistent in direction but modest in magnitude.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Six human trials with verified sample sizes totaling at least 805 participants (true total is larger, as many abstracts omit size) provide direct evidence. A single meta-analysis supports the conclusion, but no independent confirmation exists yet, limiting confidence to Moderate.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: All 10 human trials focused on this outcome. Large recent RCTs (2024: n=404, n=144, n=126; 2019: n=199) examined adding S. boulardii to standard antibiotic regimens (triple therapy, dual therapy, bismuth quadruple therapy). A 2025 meta-analysis pooled these results. Across trials, the yeast consistently improved H. pylori eradication rates (higher clearance of the bacteria) and sometimes reduced adverse effects from antibiotics. The 2024 trial with n=404 was adequately powered and showed a clear benefit.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Ten human RCTs, several with large sample sizes (100–400 participants), all point in the same direction. A single meta-analysis exists but lacks independent replication. Consistency is high within the retrieved set, but reliance on one pooled analysis keeps the grade at Moderate rather than Strong.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Eight human trials and six animal studies examined immune markers (antibody levels, immune cell counts, cytokine production) when S. boulardii was given alone or with antibiotics. Most human trials were in H. pylori-infected or heart failure patients. Studies reported improvements in specific immune markers—for example, enhanced IgA antibodies (a defense molecule in the gut), increased T-cell activity, and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines (immune signaling molecules). Animal models reinforced these findings. However, the clinical significance of these immune changes (whether they translate to fewer infections or faster recovery) is rarely tested.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate evidence includes eight human trials, but most are secondary analyses of studies designed for other outcomes (like H. pylori clearance). No single large trial was powered for immune function alone. A meta-analysis supports the pattern, but independent replication is absent. The data show immune effects; the clinical meaning remains uncertain.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Four human trials (n=21 to n=151) and 15 animal studies measured inflammatory markers or tissue inflammation. In humans, the yeast reduced inflammatory markers in IBS patients (n=21), heart failure patients (n=151), and obese patients with knee osteoarthritis (n=70). Animal models tested inflammation in viral infection (parvovirus in dogs), radiation damage in rats, and other inflammatory conditions, consistently showing reduced inflammation and improved tissue healing. Human sample sizes are small; animal models are more numerous but do not establish human benefit.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Only four human trials, with limited sample sizes and no independently replicated meta-analysis, provide modest precision. A 2025 meta-analysis exists, but several human studies remain unconfirmed. Animal data is promising for mechanism but does not prove efficacy in people. Consistency among the human trials is good, but the body of human evidence is small.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence base is mixed: Moderate grades rest on 6–10 human RCTs (mostly recent, 2013–2026) and a supporting 2025 meta-analysis, alongside 6–15 animal studies per outcome. Human trials are short-term (weeks to 3–4 months), focus on specific conditions (H. pylori infection, IBS, heart failure, neonatal jaundice, osteoarthritis), and involve at most 400 participants in a single study. The reliance on one meta-analysis per outcome, without independent confirmation, is the primary reason grades do not reach Strong. Animal evidence is consistent and mechanistically informative but does not substitute for human trials.
explanation.open_questions: The retrieved records show no trials in healthy individuals taking the supplement for general gut health—all human studies enrolled patients with a specific condition. Long-term safety (beyond 4 months) is not addressed in the retrieved trials. No data exist for immunocompromised patients, pregnant or breastfeeding women, or children beyond the single neonatal study. Whether the immune and inflammatory benefits seen in trials translate to clinically meaningful outcomes (fewer infections, faster symptom resolution, hospitalization rates) remains largely untested. The records show a clear pattern but leave open whether the effects persist, how large they are in the real world, and which populations benefit most.

appraisal.headline: The evidence base rests heavily on a single unreplicated meta-analysis, with most human trials focused on H. pylori eradication as adjunctive therapy rather than standalone gut health, and a large animal/mechanistic literature that does not reliably translate to the clinical outcomes claimed.

concerns.detail: All three outcomes (gut/digestion, H. pylori, immune function) note explicitly that 'a single meta-analysis/systematic review exists, but its conclusion is not independently replicated or verified.' For H. pylori and immune function, this one 2025 meta-analysis is the only synthesis-level evidence in a field where pooled estimates should be independently confirmed. This single study determines the 'Moderate' grade; if it has methodological flaws or narrow inclusion criteria, the grade collapses.

concerns.issue: Heavy reliance on adjunctive H. pylori trials, not monotherapy
concerns.detail: Of 7 RCTs in the H. pylori outcome, all appear to test S. boulardii *combined with* antibiotic regimens (triple therapy, bismuth quadruple therapy, vonoprazan-amoxicillin dual therapy), not as a standalone intervention. Trial titles explicitly state 'combined with' or 'plus' therapy. This means the evidence answers 'does S. boulardii improve antibiotic efficacy?' not 'does S. boulardii treat or prevent H. pylori infection?' The mechanistic claim (immune/microbiota modulation) may be confounded by the antibiotic effect.

concerns.issue: Majority of inflammation literature is animal-only (14 of 19 studies)
concerns.detail: The inflammation outcome includes only 4 human studies (2 RCTs with n=70 and n=151, plus 2 unclassified with unreported or very small n=21) against 15 animal studies. The animal literature examines models like colitis, seizure-induced neuroinflammation, radioactive iodine damage, and ovalbumin-induced pyroptosis—none of which are routine clinical conditions. The jump from rodent colitis or canine infection to human inflammatory benefit is large and unvalidated.

concerns.issue: Gut/digestion outcome conflates multiple distinct conditions without pooled analysis
concerns.detail: The 'gut/digestion' outcome mixes neonatal hyperbilirubinemia (n=119, 2015), diarrhea-predominant IBS (n=21, 2013; animal model n=60, 2026), heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (n=151, 2021), and radioactive-iodine GI damage (animal). No pooled effect is extractable, and the engine notes 'inconsistency: several studies exist but no pooled analysis confirms they agree.' These are biologically and clinically distinct indications; lumping them under 'gut/digestion' obscures heterogeneity.

concerns.issue: Majority of abstracts omit sample size; true total n is unknown
concerns.detail: For gut/digestion, 14 of 21 studies do not report n in the abstract (only 7 report: 10, 21, 60, 119, 144, 151, 300). For inflammation, 12 of 19 omit n. The engine notes 'most abstracts omit sample size, so the true total is substantially larger.' Without full data, the actual precision and whether small studies cluster around positive findings cannot be assessed. This hides potential small-study bias.

appraisal.mechanism_check: The proposed mechanisms (immune modulation via IL-17/Cyba signaling, microbiota restoration, anti-inflammatory metabolite production) are plausible in vitro and in rodent models, but the leap to human clinical benefit is large. Most human trials test S. boulardii in the *presence* of antibiotics (H. pylori trials) or in non-gut-specific conditions (heart failure, hyperbilirubinemia), so whether the mechanism operates independently in humans is unclear. The animal inflammation literature (seizures, colitis, radioactive damage) does not obviously predict benefit in common human GI or immune disorders.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would argue that (1) the H. pylori RCTs do not isolate S. boulardii's effect—they show it improves *antibiotic* outcomes, which is not the same as proving the probiotic works on its own; (2) the single unreplicated meta-analysis could be a false positive if it used loose inclusion criteria or had publication bias; and (3) the inflammation and immune outcomes rest almost entirely on animal studies of exotic models (radiation, seizures, engineered engineered strains) that have not proven predictive in humans. The Moderate grade may reflect absence of evidence of harm rather than presence of evidence of benefit.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: Independent replication of the 2025 meta-analysis with pre-registered methods and sensitivity analyses would strengthen confidence in pooled estimates. RCTs testing S. boulardii monotherapy (without antibiotics) in well-defined human populations—e.g., IBS-D, antibiotic-associated diarrhea, or inflammatory bowel disease—with blinding, adequate n (>100 per arm), and pre-specified outcomes would directly address whether the organism has independent clinical utility.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Una cepa de levadura beneficiosa utilizada como suplemento probiótico vivo para la salud intestinal.
explanation_es.what_it_is: Saccharomyces boulardii es una cepa de levadura de panadería—un hongo unicelular—que sobrevive el paso por tu estómago y se establece en el intestino delgado. A diferencia de la mayoría de los probióticos, que son bacterias, esta es una levadura. Se toma como un suplemento vivo en forma de cápsula o polvo, a menudo liofilizado para que las células permanezcan viables hasta que lleguen a tu intestino.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Secreta compuestos que reducen las bacterias dañinas y calman la inflamación intestinal.
explanation_es.how_it_works: La levadura produce sustancias que inhiben o matan bacterias patógenas (causantes de enfermedad)—notablemente Helicobacter pylori, que causa úlceras estomacales—y libera moléculas que reducen la respuesta inflamatoria en el revestimiento de tu intestino. También parece fortalecer la barrera entre tus células intestinales, reduciendo el 'intestino permeable' donde partículas no deseadas atraviesan hacia el torrente sanguíneo. Además, puede cambiar la composición de tu microbiota (los billones de microorganismos en tu intestino) hacia un equilibrio más saludable, y algunas pruebas sugieren que potencia la actividad de células inmunológicas que viven en la pared intestinal. Los mecanismos exactos no están completamente mapeados, pero el patrón entre estudios apunta tanto a acciones antimicrobianas directas como a efectos inmunomoderadores.
explanation_es.safety_line: Bien tolerada en ensayos a corto plazo; la seguridad a largo plazo y los riesgos en poblaciones específicas permanecen sin testar.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos en humanos recuperados reportaron eventos adversos leves o ninguno; la mayoría de los estudios duraron semanas a pocos meses. Sin embargo, los ensayos incluyeron solo adultos sanos y algunos grupos de pacientes específicos (p. ej., pacientes infectados con H. pylori, pacientes con insuficiencia cardíaca), y ninguno abordó adecuadamente el uso a largo plazo más allá de algunas semanas. Saccharomyces boulardii es un organismo vivo, y el perfil de seguridad en individuos inmunodeprimidos, embarazo y lactancia permanece desconocido.
safety_bullets: Pacientes inmunodeprimidos (VIH avanzado, con inmunosupresores para trasplante de órganos): sin testar; el riesgo teórico de infección por levadura no está establecido en ensayos.
Embarazo y lactancia: ningún ensayo en humanos recuperado; seguridad desconocida.
Interacciones farmacológicas con antifúngicos azólicos (p. ej., fluconazol): no reportado en ensayos recuperados; el potencial de antagonismo directo no ha sido examinado.
Seguridad pediátrica: un ensayo en neonatos (recién nacidos) encontró beneficio para la ictericia, pero el uso más amplio en niños y adolescentes está poco estudiado.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: Saccharomyces boulardii es un organismo grande y complejo (una célula eucariota, lo que significa que tiene un núcleo y organelos como las propias células), por lo que no se comporta como una pequeña molécula de fármaco. No es absorbida; vive en la luz de tu intestino y eventualmente es eliminada. Los compuestos bioactivos que produce—ácidos grasos de cadena corta, péptidos antimicrobianos y moléculas de señalización inmunológica—son lo que realmente entra en tu torrente sanguíneo, mientras que la levadura misma permanece localizada en el intestino.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Seis ensayos en humanos y un metanálisis de 2025 examinaron el efecto de la levadura en la digestión, la erradicación de H. pylori, la ictericia neonatal, el síndrome del intestino irritable y la insuficiencia cardíaca. Los estudios variaron desde pequeños ensayos abiertos (n=21) hasta un gran ECA (n=151). Cuando se agregó a la terapia con antibióticos para H. pylori, la levadura mejoró las tasas de erradicación y la recuperación de la microbiota. Un ECA (n=119) en recién nacidos encontró que redujo la severidad de la ictericia. Un ensayo en IBS predominante en diarrea (n=21) reportó mejoría clínica. El ensayo de insuficiencia cardíaca de 2021 (n=151) encontró beneficio, aunque la insuficiencia cardíaca no es clásicamente un resultado de 'digestión'. Los resultados son consistentes en dirección pero modestos en magnitud.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Seis ensayos en humanos con tamaños de muestra verificados totalizando al menos 805 participantes (el total verdadero es mayor, ya que muchos resúmenes omiten el tamaño) proporcionan evidencia directa. Un único metanálisis respalda la conclusión, pero no existe confirmación independiente aún, limitando la confianza a Moderada.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Los 10 ensayos en humanos se enfocaron en este resultado. ECA recientes grandes (2024: n=404, n=144, n=126; 2019: n=199) examinaron agregar S. boulardii a regímenes de antibióticos estándar (terapia triple, terapia dual, terapia cuádruple con bismuto). Un metanálisis de 2025 agrupó estos resultados. En todos los ensayos, la levadura mejoró consistentemente las tasas de erradicación de H. pylori (mayor aclaración de la bacteria) y a veces redujo los efectos adversos de los antibióticos. El ensayo de 2024 con n=404 fue adecuadamente potenciado y mostró un beneficio claro.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Diez ECA en humanos, varios con tamaños de muestra grandes (100–400 participantes), todos apuntan en la misma dirección. Existe un único metanálisis pero carece de replicación independiente. La consistencia es alta dentro del conjunto recuperado, pero la dependencia de un análisis agrupado mantiene la calificación en Moderada en lugar de Fuerte.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Ocho ensayos en humanos y seis estudios en animales examinaron marcadores inmunológicos (niveles de anticuerpos, conteos de células inmunológicas, producción de citoquinas) cuando S. boulardii fue administrada sola o con antibióticos. La mayoría de los ensayos en humanos fueron en pacientes infectados con H. pylori o con insuficiencia cardíaca. Los estudios reportaron mejoras en marcadores inmunológicos específicos—por ejemplo, anticuerpos IgA mejorados (una molécula de defensa en el intestino), aumento de la actividad de células T y reducción de citoquinas proinflamatorias (moléculas de señalización inmunológica). Los modelos animales reforzaron estos hallazgos. Sin embargo, la importancia clínica de estos cambios inmunológicos (si se traducen en menos infecciones o recuperación más rápida) rara vez se prueba.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La evidencia Moderada incluye ocho ensayos en humanos, pero la mayoría son análisis secundarios de estudios diseñados para otros resultados (como la erradicación de H. pylori). Ningún ensayo grande único fue potenciado para la función inmunológica sola. Un metanálisis respalda el patrón, pero la replicación independiente está ausente. Los datos muestran efectos inmunológicos; el significado clínico permanece incierto.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cuatro ensayos en humanos (n=21 a n=151) y 15 estudios en animales midieron marcadores inflamatorios o inflamación tisular. En humanos, la levadura redujo marcadores inflamatorios en pacientes con IBS (n=21), pacientes con insuficiencia cardíaca (n=151) y pacientes obesos con osteoartritis de rodilla (n=70). Los modelos animales probaron inflamación en infección viral (parvovirus en perros), daño por radiación en ratas y otras condiciones inflamatorias, mostrando consistentemente inflamación reducida y curación tisular mejorada. Los tamaños de muestra humanos son pequeños; los modelos animales son más numerosos pero no establecen beneficio en humanos.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solo cuatro ensayos en humanos, con tamaños de muestra limitados y sin metanálisis replicada independientemente, proporcionan precisión modesta. Un metanálisis de 2025 existe, pero varios estudios en humanos permanecen sin confirmar. Los datos en animales son prometedores para el mecanismo pero no prueban eficacia en personas. La consistencia entre los ensayos en humanos es buena, pero el cuerpo de evidencia en humanos es pequeño.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La base de evidencia es mixta: las calificaciones Moderada descansan en 6–10 ECA en humanos (principalmente recientes, 2013–2026) y un metanálisis de apoyo de 2025, junto con 6–15 estudios en animales por resultado. Los ensayos en humanos son a corto plazo (semanas a 3–4 meses), se enfocaron en condiciones específicas (infección por H. pylori, IBS, insuficiencia cardíaca, ictericia neonatal, osteoartritis) e involucraron como máximo 400 participantes en un solo estudio. La dependencia de un metanálisis por resultado, sin confirmación independiente, es la razón principal por la que las calificaciones no alcanzan Fuerte. La evidencia en animales es consistente e informativamente mecanística pero no sustituye los ensayos en humanos.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros recuperados muestran ningún ensayo en individuos sanos tomando el suplemento para la salud intestinal general—todos los estudios en humanos inscribieron pacientes con una condición específica. La seguridad a largo plazo (más allá de 4 meses) no se aborda en los ensayos recuperados. No existen datos para pacientes inmunodeprimidos, mujeres embarazadas o en lactancia, o niños más allá del único estudio neonatal. Si los beneficios inmunológicos e inflamatorios observados en ensayos se traducen en resultados clínicamente significativos (menos infecciones, resolución más rápida de síntomas, tasas de hospitalización) permanece en gran medida sin testar. Los registros muestran un patrón claro pero dejan abierto si los efectos persisten, cuán grandes son en el mundo real y qué poblaciones se benefician más.

appraisal_es.headline: La base de evidencia descansa pesadamente en un único metanálisis no replicado, con la mayoría de ensayos humanos enfocados en la erradicación de H. pylori como terapia adyuvante en lugar de salud intestinal independiente, y una amplia literatura animal/mecanicista que no se traduce de manera confiable en los resultados clínicos reclamados.

concerns.issue: Un único metanálisis no replicado ancla la calificación
concerns.detail: Los tres resultados (salud intestinal/digestión, H. pylori, función inmunológica) señalan explícitamente que 'existe un único metanálisis/revisión sistemática, pero su conclusión no ha sido replicada o verificada de forma independiente.' Para H. pylori y función inmunológica, este único metanálisis de 2025 es la única evidencia a nivel de síntesis en un campo donde las estimaciones agrupadas deberían ser confirmadas de forma independiente. Este estudio único determina la calificación 'Moderada'; si tiene defectos metodológicos o criterios de inclusión estrechos, la calificación se desmorona.

concerns.issue: Dependencia pesada de ensayos adyuvantes de H. pylori, no monoterapia
concerns.detail: De los 7 ECA en el resultado de H. pylori, todos parecen probar S. boulardii *combinado con* regímenes de antibióticos (terapia triple, terapia cuádruple con bismuto, terapia dual vonoprazan-amoxicilina), no como intervención independiente. Los títulos de los ensayos explícitamente establecen 'combinado con' o 'más' terapia. Esto significa que la evidencia responde 'S. boulardii ¿mejora la eficacia de antibióticos?' no '¿S. boulardii trata o previene la infección por H. pylori?' El reclamo mecanicista (modulación inmunológica/microbiota) puede estar confundido por el efecto del antibiótico.

concerns.issue: La mayoría de la literatura de inflamación es solo en animales (14 de 19 estudios)
concerns.detail: El resultado de inflamación incluye solo 4 estudios humanos (2 ECA con n=70 y n=151, más 2 sin clasificar con n no reportado o muy pequeño n=21) contra 15 estudios en animales. La literatura en animales examina modelos como colitis, neuroinflammación inducida por convulsiones, daño por yodo radiactivo, y piroptosis inducida por ovoalbúmina—ninguno de los cuales son condiciones clínicas rutinarias. El salto de la colitis en roedores o infección canina al beneficio inflamatorio humano es grande y no validado.

concerns.issue: El resultado de salud intestinal/digestión conflúye múltiples condiciones distintas sin análisis agrupado
concerns.detail: El resultado de 'salud intestinal/digestión' mezcla hiperbilirrubinemia neonatal (n=119, 2015), síndrome de intestino irritable predominante en diarrea (n=21, 2013; modelo animal n=60, 2026), insuficiencia cardíaca con fracción de eyección reducida (n=151, 2021), y daño GI por yodo radiactivo (animal). No se puede extraer un efecto agrupado, y el motor señala 'inconsistencia: existen varios estudios pero ningún análisis agrupado confirma que estén de acuerdo.' Estas son indicaciones biológica y clínicamente distintas; agruparlas bajo 'salud intestinal/digestión' oscurece la heterogeneidad.

concerns.issue: La mayoría de resúmenes omiten el tamaño de muestra; el verdadero total de n es desconocido
concerns.detail: Para salud intestinal/digestión, 14 de 21 estudios no reportan n en el resumen (solo 7 reportan: 10, 21, 60, 119, 144, 151, 300). Para inflamación, 12 de 19 omiten n. El motor señala 'la mayoría de resúmenes omiten tamaño de muestra, por lo que el verdadero total es sustancialmente mayor.' Sin datos completos, la precisión real y si estudios pequeños se agrupan alrededor de hallazgos positivos no puede ser evaluado. Esto oculta posible sesgo de estudios pequeños.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: Los mecanismos propuestos (modulación inmunológica vía señalización IL-17/Cyba, restauración de microbiota, producción de metabolitos antiinflamatorios) son plausibles in vitro y en modelos en roedores, pero el salto al beneficio clínico humano es grande. La mayoría de ensayos humanos prueban S. boulardii *en presencia* de antibióticos (ensayos de H. pylori) o en condiciones no específicas del intestino (insuficiencia cardíaca, hiperbilirrubinemia), por lo que si el mecanismo opera independientemente en humanos es incierto. La literatura de inflamación en animales (convulsiones, colitis, daño radiactivo) no predice obviamente beneficio en trastornos GI o inmunológicos humanos comunes.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico argumentaría que (1) los ECA de H. pylori no aíslan el efecto de S. boulardii—muestran que mejora *resultados de antibióticos*, lo que no es lo mismo que probar que el probiótico funciona por sí solo; (2) el único metanálisis no replicado podría ser un falso positivo si utilizó criterios de inclusión laxos o tuvo sesgo de publicación; y (3) los resultados de inflamación e inmunidad descansan casi enteramente en estudios en animales de modelos exóticos (radiación, convulsiones, cepas diseñadas) que no han demostrado ser predictivos en humanos. La calificación Moderada puede reflejar ausencia de evidencia de daño en lugar de presencia de evidencia de beneficio.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: La replicación independiente del metanálisis de 2025 con métodos preregistrados y análisis de sensibilidad fortalecería la confianza en las estimaciones agrupadas. ECA probando S. boulardii monoterapia (sin antibióticos) en poblaciones humanas bien definidas—p.ej., SII-D, diarrea asociada a antibióticos, o enfermedad inflamatoria intestinal—con cegamiento, n adecuado (>100 por brazo), y resultados preespecificados abordarían directamente si el organismo tiene utilidad clínica independiente.
